headline: Latent and probabilistic models add spatial structure, 3D geometry and interpretability to omics
label: Spatial Omics Latent Models
summary: New spatial omics methods pair latent-variable and foundation models with 3D reconstruction, causal identifiability and statistical tests of embedding fidelity.
synthesis: The common thread is structured latent representations for spatial and single-cell omics. multiCAsp places a graph-Laplacian spatial prior on joint multi-omic factors, and CIRCA uses self-supervised causal representation learning to obtain identifiable cell and niche programs. CASTLE adds cell-type-aware spatial graphs to contrastive domain detection. A second thread is 3D and morphology-linked inference: a rotation-equivariant network reconstructs cell shape from transcript point clouds, Space-map aligns serial sections into 3D atlases, and Loki2, GenVinci and sc-HistoMorphomics link H&E images to molecular readouts. Other works address evaluation and interpretability: velotest tests RNA velocity embedding fidelity, MiSA tests spatial dysbiosis, and TMCells and the hybrid mixture model offer probabilistic, non-spatial alternatives. The emphasis falls on identifiable, interpretable spatial representations with explicit statistical assessment.
